# Technical Decisions

## ADR-001: Structured pages instead of generated code

**Accepted.** A closed component catalog and versioned Zod schema are safer to render, test and export than arbitrary JS/HTML generated by an LLM. This limits design expressiveness, but keeps generated content as data rather than executable source.

## ADR-002: Sandboxed iframe preview

**Accepted.** The same HTML renderer produces both preview and export; the iframe uses `sandbox` without script permission. This prevents code execution and isolates the site's styles from the editor interface.

## ADR-003: Local-only version storage

**Accepted for the MVP.** LocalStorage with bounded checkpoints avoids authentication/database infrastructure and keeps demos fast. Limitations include per-browser storage, lack of sync and a maximum 15 snapshot history. No false multi-device promise.

## ADR-004: Deterministic demo required

**Accepted.** Demo works without accounts or tokens and is used for all CI checks. It never claims actual AI model generation. The optional paid adapter has explicit server-side opt-in and is not tested with paid calls automatically.

## ADR-005: Static HTML/CSS export

**Accepted.** The ZIP contains a fixed set of four filenames. It works without bundling, node_modules or server infrastructure. React/Next.js source export is a possible future feature, not a claim of the MVP.

## ADR-006: No public live paid endpoint by default

**Accepted.** Allowing unauthenticated paid requests on a public deployment would invite abuse. Production is gated separately; actual public use requires a later security iteration with authentication, rate limits and quotas.
